note: Low-resolution scan (1078 px wide) but legible roman type. OCR matches the image except Patriculo→'Patruculo', a dropped 'est', dispergit'→'dispergit' and 'ardentiorsq̃'; q̃/p/em̃ were left unexpanded (fixed file expands them). The 1515 print really reads 'intuentes afflent' and 'Vides enim' where the modern text (and the reference) has 'fallant' / 'Quid enim?', so those findings are edition differences, not OCR.
